title: SDK call contract enforcer & streaming runloop adapters
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: SDK consumers need a consistent, low-friction way to call model-side tools/functions across Python/TS/Go while preserving strong typing, safety, and streaming ergonomics. Current ad-hoc approaches lead to duplicated validation logic, subtle serialization bugs (especially in Go), and brittle retry semantics when a partial stream has already been emitted.

Goal: Implement a cross-language client-side "contract enforcer" that validates and coerces user-provided function schemas + payloads before submitting to the API, plus a set of per-language runloop adapters that provide: (1) ergonomic streaming of function results (partial/streamed args), (2) robust retry/backoff semantics for idempotent calls, and (3) clear developer guidance and examples.

Scope: Python, TypeScript, Go SDKs. Deliverables: validation helpers, example generator (type hints / interfaces), runloop adapters for streaming+retries, tests, docs and example apps demonstrating edge cases (schema drift, unknown fields, partial streams).
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a consistent validation API: validate_function_contract(schema, payload) or equivalent in each language
Validation catches: missing required params, type mismatches, unknown fields (configurable strict/lenient modes), and provides helpful error messages with suggestion hints
Go SDK includes marshaler that converts JSON-ish payloads into typed structs without panics and returns deterministic error codes
Streaming runloop adapters support resumable streams for idempotent operations or provide clear developer-visible failure semantics for non-idempotent calls
Retry policy defaults are safe: retry on network and 5xx, do not retry on user-input validation errors or non-idempotent function side effects unless user opts in
Comprehensive unit/integration tests across languages and a cross-SDK end-to-end example app
Docs and a short migration guide included in SDK repo and Console examples page
decision_log: 2026-02-20: Agreed on two-layer validation: schema-level (shape & types) + runtime coercion (string->int, int->float when safe). Avoid over-eager coercion for booleans and IDs.
2026-02-25: Chose to implement 'strict' and 'lenient' modes. Default = strict for Private/Dedicated customers; lenient for quick prototyping in hosted environment.
2026-03-02: Retry policy: default exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries. Expose hooks for custom idempotency tokens. Do not replay streams automatically for non-idempotent function calls.
2026-03-08: Streaming adapter surface: provide both high-level async iterator for TS/Python and channel-based API for Go. Streams will yield 'progress' events and final 'result' event.
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Spike completed for Python + TS validation libs. Found edge cases around union types and nullability in TS that require explicit annotations.
2026-02-24: PoC runloop adapter for Python streaming implemented (async generator). Basic retry hooks added. Opened internal RFC: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=40523
2026-03-01: Go marshalers work for simple schemas; failing on nested optional arrays. Added testcases and raised bug ENG-23198 as dependency.
2026-03-05: Cross-SDK design review with PM/Design. Feedback: surface helpful error messages, include example migration snippets in Console snippets pane.

2026-03-12: Integration tests: function-calling-e2e test failing intermittently on flaky network emulation (investigating test harness). Added temporary increase to test timeout while root cause identified.
testing_plan: Unit tests for validator in each language covering positive/negative cases and coercion behavior
Property-based fuzzing for schema marshaler in Go to find panics and edge cases
Integration e2e that runs a sample app that performs: function-call with streamed partial args, fails mid-stream and exercises retry semantics
Chaos tests that inject transient network errors and verify retry/backoff is exercised but no duplicate side effects for idempotent calls
Manual UX review with Developer Relations to confirm error messaging and snippets
rollout_plan: Feature gated in SDK minor releases. Alpha enabled behind feature flag 'fn_contract_enforcer' for early customers via config on Dedicated. Roll out default strict mode to Private and Dedicated in runtime-1.21. Hosted default remains lenient for two cycles while telemetry evaluates developer errors.
risks: Overzealous coercion could mask user bugs and lead to incorrect downstream behavior
Go's strict typing increases surface area for subtle marshaling bugs; risk of panics in worst case
Retrying streamed operations can produce duplicated side effects if user functions are not idempotent
Complex migration for customers already using custom validation logic
notes: Follow-up: add a CLI tool that validates a function schema against a set of example payloads (helpful during model onboarding).
API change: appended 'validation_mode' optional param to create_function_call route — backend already accepts but SDK must pass correct defaults.
Design suggestion from DevRel: create ready-to-copy code snippets for Console showing JS/TS/Python/Go usage for both strict and lenient modes.
